prompt: Complete SerialDeepCopier.deepCopy so it copies any Serializable object by writing it to bytes and reading it back, giving a copy that shares no mutable state with the original.
explanation: Serializing an object writes its entire reachable graph, so reading it back builds brand new instances of every object in that graph -- that is what makes this a deep copy rather than the shallow field-by-field copy a naive clone would give. The generic signature <T extends Serializable> keeps the call site typed, and the unchecked cast is safe because the bytes came from a T. The cost is real: this is far slower than a hand-written copy constructor, so it is a convenience trick, not a default.
hints: You need a ByteArrayOutputStream for the write half and a ByteArrayInputStream over its bytes for the read half.
Close or flush the ObjectOutputStream before calling toByteArray, otherwise buffered bytes are missing.
readObject returns Object -- cast it to T; the method already carries a SuppressWarnings annotation because the compiler cannot verify that cast.
